intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that common variable immunodeficiency-15 (CVID15) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the SEC61A1 gene (609213) on chromosome 3q21.

checks.claim: Common variable immunodeficiency-15 (CVID15) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the SEC61A1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We found two heterozygous SEC61A1 mutations in patients of two unrelated families with an early-onset, infection-only antibody deficiency and normal (sub-)populations of peripheral B cells.
checks.explanation: The paper links heterozygous SEC61A1 mutations to primary antibody deficiency, ranging to CVID. 'CVID15' is OMIM's name for the disorder.

checks.claim: The SEC61A1 gene is located on chromosome 3q21.
checks.evidence_quote: Evaluation of all variants shared among the four affected individuals and absent in the two unaffected family members revealed three novel single-nucleotide variants (SNV) in the genes SEC61A1, GOLGA8K and SLC47A2, with only SEC61A1 located in the linkage region on chromosome 3
checks.explanation: The paper places SEC61A1 on chromosome 3. The 3q21 band is standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Common variable immunodeficiency-15 (CVID15) is a primary antibody deficiency. It is characterized by low serum IgM, IgG and IgA and by severe recurrent bacterial infections, mostly beginning in the first year of life. These include tonsillitis, otitis, sinusitis, pneumonia and gastrointestinal infections. Peripheral B-cell numbers are normal, but plasmablast and plasma cell differentiation is defective (Schubert et al., 2018).

checks.claim: CVID15 is a primary antibody deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified a novel genetic defect and studied its pathologic mechanism in 11 patients from 2 unrelated families with PADs.
checks.explanation: PAD stands for primary antibody deficiency.

checks.claim: The recurrent bacterial infections in CVID15 mostly begin in the first year of life.
checks.evidence_quote: The disease onset was mostly in the first year of life.

checks.evidence_quote: who suffered from severe recurrent bacterial infections such as tonsillitis, otitis, sinusitis, pneumonias and gastrointestinal infections

checks.evidence_quote: The differentiation of resting peripheral B cells into CD27+CD38high plasmablasts and CD38highCD138+ plasma cells was significantly decreased in mutation carriers from both families

paragraphs.text: Schubert et al. (2018) studied 10 affected individuals in a family (Family I). They had deficiencies of the IgM, IgG and IgA isotypes and severe recurrent bacterial infections, including tonsillitis, otitis, sinusitis, pneumonia and gastrointestinal infections. Onset was mostly in the first year of life. Affected individuals did not respond to polysaccharide vaccination and had variable responses to tetanus toxoid vaccination. After IVIG replacement therapy was started, infections became markedly fewer and less severe.

paragraphs.text: Schubert et al. (2018) also described a second family (Family II). The index patient (II.P3) was an 8-year-old boy who had had hypogammaglobulinemia since birth. On IVIG treatment he had no severe or recurrent infections. Repeated attempts to withdraw IVIG failed because his immunoglobulin levels stayed low. His grandmother, a mutation carrier, had more frequent upper respiratory infections and recurrent bilateral bacterial otitis media in childhood. Her serum immunoglobulin levels were normal at age 66 years.

paragraphs.text: In patients from both families, Schubert et al. (2018) found normal B-, T- and NK-cell ratios. T-cell subsets, regulatory T cells and recent thymic emigrants were normal. Peripheral B-cell subpopulations were also normal, including naive, unswitched memory, switched memory, transitional and CD21-low B cells. The only abnormality was an apparent reduction in the very small CD27+CD38-high plasmablast population in Family I. The patients had no clinical symptoms other than infections. Serum levels of liver- and pancreas-secreted proteins were normal, as were the laboratory values that are altered in SEC61A1-associated autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease (ADTKD).

paragraphs.text: Schubert et al. (2018) performed whole-exome sequencing on 4 affected and 2 unaffected members of Family I. They identified a heterozygous c.254T-A transversion in the SEC61A1 gene (609213), predicting a val85-to-asp (V85D) substitution. SEC61A1 was the only candidate gene in the chromosome 3 linkage region. Sanger sequencing confirmed that the mutation segregated perfectly with the disease. V85 is highly conserved and is one of the 6 pore-ring residues of the Sec61 channel. In HeLa cells, the V85D mutant impaired cotranslational translocation of preprolactin. Its overexpression lowered the ER calcium load, which the authors concluded was a dominant effect.

paragraphs.text: Schubert et al. (2018) then performed targeted next-generation sequencing in more than 200 additional patients with primary antibody deficiency. They identified a heterozygous c.1325G-T nonsense mutation in SEC61A1 (E381X) in the index patient of Family II. His grandmother and mother also carried the mutation. No premature stop codons in SEC61A1 were present in the gnomAD database. SEC61A1 protein was reduced in the patients' naive B cells, and no truncated protein was detected. The authors suggested that the mutation causes nonsense-mediated mRNA decay and haploinsufficiency, with variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance.

paragraphs.text: Schubert et al. (2018) found that overexpression of SEC61A1-V85D depleted the ER calcium store in HeLa cells, suggesting increased Ca(2+) leakage. In multiple myeloma cell lines, stable expression of the mutant led to loss of the transduced cells. It also activated the terminal unfolded protein response, with upregulation of IRE1A, PERK, XBP1s, ATF4 and CHOP. Other cell lines were not affected. In thapsigargin-treated HEK293T cells, the V85D mutant had a dominant effect on XBP1s induction. The authors concluded that the mutation selectively impairs plasma cell survival.

paragraphs.text: Schubert et al. (2018) studied affected members of a family (Family I) with CVID15. In these patients they identified a heterozygous c.254T-A transversion in the SEC61A1 gene, predicting a val85-to-asp (V85D) substitution at a highly conserved pore-ring residue of the Sec61 channel. The mutation was found by whole-exome sequencing and segregated perfectly with the disease, which was linked to chromosome 3. In HeLa cells, the mutant impaired cotranslational translocation of preprolactin, and its overexpression depleted the ER calcium store. In multiple myeloma cell lines, stable expression of the mutant led to loss of the transduced cells and activated the terminal unfolded protein response. In thapsigargin-treated HEK293T cells, the mutant had a dominant effect on XBP1s induction.

checks.claim: The SEC61A1 E381X mutation was not present in gnomAD.
checks.evidence_quote: there are no mutations reported in healthy individuals leading to a premature stop codon in SEC61A1
checks.explanation: Because gnomAD lists no premature-stop SEC61A1 variants, E381X is absent from it.

checks.claim: SEC61A1 protein was reduced in naive B cells of SEC61A1 E381X carriers.
checks.evidence_quote: We observed reduced expression levels of SEC61A1 in naïve B cells of II.P1 and II.P3

checks.claim: No truncated SEC61A1 protein was detected in SEC61A1 E381X carriers.
checks.evidence_quote: we excluded the presence of a shortened protein product from the mutated allele in Family II
checks.explanation: This was tested in II.P3's EBV-transformed B cell line.

checks.claim: The findings for SEC61A1 E381X suggested nonsense-mediated mRNA decay and haploinsufficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: supporting the hypothesis that the nonsense mutation p.E381* likely results in nonsense-mediated mRNA decay and leads to SEC61A1 haploinsufficiency in Family II

checks.claim: The findings for SEC61A1 E381X suggested variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance.
checks.evidence_quote: We suggest that SEC61A1 haploinsufficincy is causing (possibly transient) hypogammaglobulinemia with variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance in Family II.
